english.html: ther, called Valentin Rougié, who named him and recognised him as du Tilh, he made a sign with his finger that he should hold his peace. To the third, called Pelegrin de Liberos, he made a like sign and moreover gave two handkerchiefs, with the charge to deliver one to Jean du Tilh his brother.

If these witnesses had not been singular, each deposing to his own fact, and well objected to, this proof alone would indeed have been sufficient to put him to the torture [géhenne]. For although a confession of a crime, made out of judgment, is not sufficient to condemn a man, without a new trial, or else extraordinarily at the discretion of the Judge, as a fool, vainglorious and overweening, having boasted of doing ill a: nevertheless it makes a sufficient indication for putting such a rustic, who has confessed, to the torture b.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 5.31 (De excessibus praelatorum et subditorum), c. Quam sit grave (chapter number unverified)
notes.original: c. quàm ſit graue. de ex. ceſ. prelato
notes.gloss: Cited for the rule that a confession made out of court does not of itself convict, but may draw an extraordinary penalty on the boaster; the print's prelato has a plain e for praelato.

notes.citation: Accursius (Accurſe), the Gloss on Digest 48.5 (Ad legem Iuliam de adulteriis coercendis), l. Capite quinto (fragment number unverified)
notes.original: Accurſe en la l. capite quinto- D. de adult,
notes.gloss: The extrajudicial confession as an indicium sufficient for torture.

english.html: Sixthly, two other witnesses depose that a soldier from Rochefort, not long ago, passed through the place of Artigat, who, astonished to see the said du Tilh call himself Martin Guerre, said aloud that he was a trickster: for Martin Guerre was in Flanders, having only one leg, and the other of wood, for having lost the one from a cannon-shot before Saint-Quentin, on St Lawrence's day.
Although this proof was not very necessary, because a testimony of having heard say [hearsay] proves nothing <sup class="mk" data-key="a2">a2</sup>; nevertheless when the true Martin Guerre arri

notes.citation: Decretals, X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Iam litteris (as printed; chapter not identified) and c. Licet ex quadam (cf. X 2.20.47, Innocent III, on witnesses who depose from hearsay; number unverified); X 4.14 (De consanguinitate et affinitate), c. Tutela (the print's rutela; chapter number unverified)
notes.original: c. iam literis. c, licet ex quadam, deſti. c. rutela. de. conſan. & affini,
notes.gloss: Deſti. is the print's contraction for de teſti[bus]; rutela is a wrong sort for tutela. Cited for the rule that testimony de auditu makes no proof.
